transcript:
[doctor] Hi Ms. Williams, how are you today?
[patient] Hey Doc, I'm alright, but I've been having some troubling episodes lately.
[doctor] Hmm, I see. Can you tell me more about these episodes?
[patient] Sure. I’ve been having these syncope episodes where I just collapse. They happen about once a week and have been going on for the past month.
[doctor] That sounds concerning. How long do these episodes last?
[patient] Just a couple of minutes, but they feel much longer.
[doctor] I can imagine. Do you experience any symptoms before or during these episodes?
[patient] Yes, I get short of breath, my vision gets blurry, and I feel nauseated.
[doctor] Have these episodes affected your daily activities?
[patient] Definitely. I’ve had to stop whatever I’m doing because I’m afraid of collapsing.
[doctor] That must be very disruptive. Have you noticed anything that seems to trigger these episodes?
[patient] Not really. They seem to come out of nowhere.
[doctor] Okay. Let’s talk a little about your sleep. How have you been sleeping lately?
[patient] Not well. I struggle with insomnia and only get about 4-5 hours of sleep per night.
[doctor] I see. How is your diet?
[patient] I try to eat a high-protein, low-carb diet.
[doctor] What about physical activity?
[patient] I do light yoga three times a week, and I enjoy gardening and playing chess.
[doctor] That’s good to hear. Do you smoke or drink alcohol?
[patient] Yes, I smoke about a pack of cigarettes per week and drink 3-4 glasses of wine per week.
[doctor] Thank you for sharing that information. Let’s review your medical history. I see you have asthma and hyperlipidemia. Are there any other medical conditions we should know about?
[patient] No, just those two.
[doctor] And what medications are you currently taking?
[patient] I take an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma and Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for hyperlipidemia.
[doctor] Alright, let’s go over your symptoms in detail. You mentioned shortness of breath and blurred vision during the syncope episodes. Any other issues with your eyes or vision?
[patient] No, just the blurred vision during the episodes.
[doctor] How about your respiratory system? Any other symptoms like cough or chest pain?
[patient] I have wheezing, especially when I breathe out forcefully, but no cough or chest pain.
[doctor] Any chest pain or palpitations at all?
[patient] No, none.
[doctor] Do you experience nausea outside of these syncope episodes?
[patient] No, just during the episodes.
[doctor] How about abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits?
[patient] None of that.
[doctor] What about headaches, seizures, or any other neurological symptoms?
[patient] No headaches or seizures, just the syncope and blurred vision.
[doctor] Are you feeling depressed or anxious about these episodes?
[patient] No, but I am definitely concerned about them.
[doctor] Understandably so. Let’s take your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, respiratory rate is 18/min, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Your oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Everything looks normal. Now, I’ll conduct a physical exam. You’re alert and oriented, and you don’t appear to be in any acute distress.
[doctor] Listening to your heart, I hear normal S1 and S2 sounds with no murmurs. Your heart rhythm is regular.
[doctor] When I listen to your lungs, I hear wheezes bilaterally, especially on forced expiration.
[doctor] Checking your neurological status, your cranial nerves II-XII are intact, and you have no motor or sensory deficits.
[doctor] Your abdomen is soft, non-tender, and there’s no organomegaly.
[doctor] Your extremities have no edema, and your peripheral pulses are good.
[doctor] Based on your symptoms and our examination, I’m considering several possibilities for your syncope episodes, including vasovagal syncope, cardiac arrhythmias, and neurological causes.
[doctor] I want to run some tests to get a clearer picture. We’ll start with an ECG to check for any arrhythmias.
[patient] Okay, that makes sense.
[doctor] We’ll also do a Tilt-table test to evaluate for vasovagal syncope and an MRI of your brain to rule out any structural abnormalities.
[patient] Alright, I understand.
[doctor] Additionally, I’d like to do some blood work, including a Complete Blood Count (CBC) and a Biochemistry Panel.
[patient] Sure, whatever you think is necessary.
[doctor] I’m also going to refer you to a neurologist, Dr. Linda Garcia, for further evaluation.
[patient] Okay, I’ll see her.
[doctor] In the meantime, we need to ensure you stay hydrated and maintain your electrolyte balance. Drinking oral rehydration salts can help with that.
[patient] I’ll get those.
[doctor] Continue taking your inhaled corticosteroid for asthma and Atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia.
[patient] Will do.
[doctor] We should also discuss some lifestyle modifications. Smoking cessation and reducing alcohol intake would be beneficial.
[patient] I’ll work on that.
[doctor] Improving your sleep hygiene can help address the insomnia. Try to maintain a regular sleep schedule and create a relaxing bedtime routine.
[patient] I’ll give that a try.
[doctor] We’ll follow up in one week to review your initial test results. Then we’ll meet again in a month to assess how the treatment is working and make any necessary adjustments.
[patient] That sounds good, Doctor.
[doctor] Do you have any questions or concerns right now?
[patient] No questions at the moment. I just hope we can figure out what’s going on.
[doctor] We’ll do our best to get to the bottom of this. Thank you for coming in today, Ms. Williams.
[patient] Thank you, Doctor.
